# shadcn/ui (Radix) adapter

**Status:** Experimental
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0
**Implementation reviewed:** shadcn CLI 4.21.0 on 2026-09-11

This adapter maps the source-distributed shadcn/ui model to GOV.UK services with an explicitly selected Radix base. Locally owned shadcn-style primitives may support supplementary service-owned interactions, while GOV.UK Frontend CSS, JavaScript and official markup remain mandatory fallbacks whenever a shadcn component cannot preserve the GOV.UK DOM, state or behaviour contract. A copied component or themed primitive is not evidence of GOV.UK conformance.

## Compatibility level

- `guidance`
- `token`
- `markup`
- `behaviour-tested`

These levels describe this adapter's bounded evidence. They do not mean that shadcn CLI itself supplies GOV.UK components, that a service is accessible, or that a theme makes an implementation conformant.

## Scope and requirements

- Treat shadcn/ui as source code that the service owns and reviews, not a sealed component dependency or a GOV.UK component library. Registry output can change independently of the CLI version, so inspect and commit every generated file and dependency change.
- Use GOV.UK Frontend CSS, JavaScript and official markup for GOV.UK components. If a shadcn or Radix primitive changes the documented elements, `govuk-*` classes, IDs, ARIA relationships, state model or progressive-enhancement behaviour, use the official GOV.UK markup instead of adapting the primitive.
- Limit shadcn-style primitives to clearly service-owned interactions with no applicable GOV.UK component or to composition around an untouched official component. Essential service tasks and content must remain available when the primitive JavaScript does not run.
- Use the applicable React adapter's server-rendering, hydration and immutable GOV.UK Frontend boundary. A Radix portal can manage its own subtree, but React must not reconcile DOM that GOV.UK Frontend has enhanced.
- Confirm separately that the service may use GDS Transport, the GOV.UK crown and other protected identity assets. This adapter maps neither a font family nor identity artwork.

## Installation and build order

- Pin the reviewed toolchain with `npm install --save-dev --save-exact shadcn@4.21.0` and the fixture runtime with `npm install --save-dev --save-exact radix-ui@1.6.7 cn@0.2.6`. The fixture also uses the repository's exact React 19.3.0, React DOM 19.3.0, Tailwind CSS 4.3.3, Tailwind CLI 4.3.3 and GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 versions.
- New shadcn projects default to Base UI as of July 2026. Select the still-supported Radix base explicitly with `npx shadcn@4.21.0 init --base radix`; do not rely on the changing default. Existing projects should keep their reviewed base unless a separate migration is planned and tested.
- Add only the primitive needed for the service-owned interaction, review the generated registry source and dependency diff, and keep the result in application source control. Do not bulk-add a parallel shadcn implementation of the GOV.UK component inventory.
- Copy GOV.UK Frontend assets to stable local application URLs and load the layered shadcn/Tailwind stylesheet before unlayered GOV.UK Frontend CSS. Never hotlink registry, Tailwind or GOV.UK Design System assets in production.

## Preflight and cascade

- A standard shadcn Tailwind setup may use `@import "tailwindcss"`, which injects Tailwind Preflight. Do not keep that one-line import beside GOV.UK Frontend; import Tailwind theme and utilities individually and omit `tailwindcss/preflight.css`. Declare `box-border` explicitly on locally owned overlays whose measured width includes padding and borders.
- Keep copied shadcn utility rules in named cascade layers and GOV.UK Frontend CSS unlayered. Keep Tailwind utilities off the internal DOM of official components and do not use `important` to force a shadcn style over a GOV.UK selector.
- Review registry updates for global CSS variables, element rules, reset imports, animation plugins and semantic token changes before accepting them. Disabling Tailwind Preflight does not neutralise a reset or baseline introduced by copied registry code or another library.

## Token mapping

- The generated `shadcn/govuk-theme.css` is an independently installable copy of the reviewed GOV.UK Tailwind token bridge, produced from the canonical token JSON rather than hand-maintained values. It exists separately so selecting shadcn does not silently select the Tailwind adapter.
- Use namespaced utilities such as `bg-govuk-surface`, `border-govuk-text`, `outline-govuk-focus`, `gap-govuk-4` and `p-govuk-responsive-6` only in locally owned shadcn-style source. These utilities expose values, not GOV.UK semantics or component rules.
- Do not alias generic shadcn theme names such as `primary`, `destructive`, `muted` or `radius` to GOV.UK values and infer equivalent meaning. Make each service-owned mapping explicit, and do not map a font family or rounded-corner scale that the reviewed GOV.UK tokens do not provide.
- Keep complete utility class names in copied source or register explicit `@source` paths. Audit every regenerated class list when the shadcn registry source changes.

## Official components and behaviour

- Use the official GOV.UK Button, Text input, Accordion and every other documented GOV.UK component when the shadcn equivalent cannot retain the exact GOV.UK contract. A matching component name or appearance is never enough to claim markup compatibility.
- A locally owned Radix Alert Dialog can be considered when an important service-owned decision genuinely requires interruption and protected focus and no applicable GOV.UK component exists. Supply a visible title and description, clearly distinguished keep and destructive actions, Escape dismissal, focus containment and focus return; provide a normal no-JavaScript route for the same decision.
- The reference fixture composes Radix Alert Dialog Trigger, Cancel and Action around explicit controls with `asChild`, but does not replace Button, Text input or Accordion with registry components. Its three fallback sections are deliberately labelled so the boundary is visible in code and in the rendered evidence.
- Initialise GOV.UK Frontend only inside the stable React boundary. Test Alert Dialog pointer, Enter, Escape, initial cancel focus, tab containment and focus return separately from GOV.UK Accordion pointer, Enter, focus, validation relationships and no-JavaScript content.

## Browser support

- Use the intersection of the host React, Radix, Tailwind and GOV.UK Frontend support ranges. Radix documents testing across modern browsers and assistive technologies, while Tailwind CSS 4 requires Safari 16.4, Chrome 111 or Firefox 128 or newer; that presentation baseline is narrower than GOV.UK Frontend's progressive-enhancement range.
- Keep essential task structure, content and official component styling in GOV.UK Frontend so users outside the shadcn/Tailwind enhancement baseline can still complete the service. Do not promote this fixture's successful browser run into a general browser-support claim.
- Re-run keyboard, screen-reader and browser tests whenever shadcn registry source, `radix-ui`, React, Tailwind or GOV.UK Frontend changes. Source ownership means upstream accessibility fixes are not received until the copied component is reviewed and updated.

## Build example

Import Tailwind theme and utilities explicitly, omit Preflight, load the generated shadcn bridge, and scan only locally owned application source containing complete class names:

```css
@layer theme, base, components, utilities;

@import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme);
@import "./ui-frameworks/shadcn/govuk-theme.css";
@import "tailwindcss/utilities.css" layer(utilities) source(none);

@source "./src/components/ui";
@source "./src/features";
```

Use a locally owned Radix primitive only for a protected cancellation decision that genuinely requires interruption, then fall back to untouched official GOV.UK markup when the similarly named shadcn component cannot preserve the GOV.UK contract:

```jsx
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
    <button className="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary" type="button">
      Cancel this form
    </button>
  </AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Cancel and lose your answers?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>Your unsaved answers will be cleared.</AlertDialogDescription>
    <AlertDialogCancel asChild>
      <button className="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary" type="button">Keep my answers</button>
    </AlertDialogCancel>
    <AlertDialogAction asChild>
      <a className="govuk-button govuk-button--warning" href="/cancelled" role="button">Cancel and lose answers</a>
    </AlertDialogAction>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

<div className="govuk-accordion" data-module="govuk-accordion" id="guidance">
  <div className="govuk-accordion__section">
    {/* Copy the remaining official Accordion DOM, IDs and classes exactly. */}
  </div>
</div>
```

## Reference fixture

The development fixture starts with `npm run fixture:serve:shadcn` and renders a React 19.3.0 server page on port 4179. It bundles a locally owned shadcn-style Alert Dialog wrapper over `radix-ui@1.6.7`, compiles the independently installable GOV.UK Tailwind bridge without Preflight, and loads that layered CSS before unlayered GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 CSS. The protected confirmation interrupts cancellation before fixture answers are lost and has an equivalent no-JavaScript confirmation route; it does not claim to be a live service. Button, Text input and Accordion are explicit official-markup fallbacks. Browser evidence must cover Alert Dialog pointer, Enter, Escape, initial cancel focus, focus containment and focus return plus the retained GOV.UK Accordion pointer, keyboard, focus and no-JavaScript contract. The fixture is test evidence, not package payload or a starter application.
